//1: claude-watch-approve config. Edit this file to tune behavior.
//2: All fields optional; sane defaults are baked into the hook too.
//port: Port of the Mac companion HTTP bridge (localhost only).
//health: Connect timeout for GET /health. Kept short so an offline bridge falls back to the terminal prompt FAST.
//req: Overall timeout for the blocking POST /permission. Should be >= the bridge's own ~60s watch timeout so we let the watch win the race.
//routing2: Decision order for every tool call: (1) if the tool is NOT in route_tools -> auto-allow, skip watch. (2) else if it matches an auto_allow rule -> auto-allow, skip watch. (3) else -> send to watch.
//route_tools: Only these tools are ever routed to the watch. Everything else (Read, Grep, Glob, LS, TodoWrite, Task, etc.) auto-allows without buzzing. Note: the settings.json matcher should mirror this list so the hook is not even invoked for other tools.

auto_allow.//: Tools/commands that skip the watch even though they are in route_tools.
auto_allow.//bash: If a Bash command's normalized text STARTS WITH any of these prefixes (token-aware), it auto-allows. Keep these read-only / non-destructive. Matching is prefix-on-token-boundary so 'catalog' does NOT match 'cat'.
auto_allow.//tool_names: Any tool name listed here always auto-allows even if in route_tools.

//cache: Where 'don't ask again' (scope:always) approval rules persist. Delete this file to clear all remembered approvals.
//failopen: false (recommended) => when bridge/watch is unreachable, return 'ask' (fall back to terminal prompt). true => return 'allow' (dangerous; never auto-approve on infra failure). Leave false.
